prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 252 Part B: the AGN luminosity-function gate (docs/agn-luminosity-function-gate): a quasar luminosity function by 1/Vmax from a flux-limited catalogue subset, with the sample's completeness and K-corrections, against a published function pinned as the oracle
committed: before any catalogue row, completeness document, K-correction, published luminosity function, estimator code or oracle output for this gate exists in the tree. Nothing of the catalogue has been read, typed or fetched.
rule: 7.5 rule 3 and 4: a gate commits its thresholds first. A threshold that proves unmeasurable fails the gate on that threshold and only Carl resets it. A data-rights decision is per source and per intended redistribution form. A leg whose catalogue, completeness document, K-correction source or published function is absent is NOT RUN (Carl's delegation, 2026-11-05): until the files arrive there is no verdict, nothing is built within one, and the consumers take the C alternative (a reading step). No luminosity-function value, K-correction, selection limit, area, catalogue column name or licence term is typed from memory; none is fetched by the session that wrote this file. A luminosity function is never presented without its completeness correction and K-correction.

verdictRule.A: G1 to G6 pass: a luminosity function by 1/Vmax with intervals, the completeness correction and the K-correction stated
verdictRule.B: G1, G2 and G7 pass and any of G3 to G6 fails: the Malmquist demonstration on the sample without a luminosity function (the mean luminosity of the flux-limited sample against redshift, with the limiting luminosity curve); nothing else is built
verdictRule.C: G1 or G2 fails (or the sample cannot be redistributed): a reading step
verdictRule.notDecided: any of G1, G2, G3 or G7 NOT RUN: no verdict, and the effective state for consumers is C until the legs run

needs.sample: one SDSS quasar catalogue subset (exact product and data release, the columns and rows used, the selection and its flux limit, the survey area, the redistribution terms read with a retrieval date, the file's SHA-256) with the sample's completeness documentation as a function of magnitude and redshift
needs.kCorrection: one named K-correction source (a published continuum-and-lines recipe or table, its version and licence read, its SHA-256) for the band the sample is selected in
needs.oracle: one published luminosity function for the same band, redshift bins and cosmology, in a table with its terms read, pinned as the oracle; the bins and the cosmology conversion are recorded
needs.completenessObject: 154's selection-function object (js/kernels/statistics/selection.js) carries the completeness; no separate completeness code is written

checks.what: the sample's product, release, columns, selection, flux limit, area, redistribution terms with a retrieval date and the SHA-256 are recorded and the file is present with a rights basis accepted under rule 4 (public domain, CC BY, or a stated no-licence-credited basis as its own decision); the analysis reads no value that is not in the file

the sample's completeness as a function of apparent magnitude and redshift is documented by the survey and loaded into the selection-function object; the correction and its uncertainty are applied to every bin, never omitted

the K-correction's source, its band and the redshift range of its validity are recorded; a source outside its range is refused; the K-correction is applied by the pinned source's own recipe and compared with the source's stated example values to a relative 1e-3 where it states any

the 1/Vmax luminosity function (with the completeness correction and the K-correction) against the pinned published function in every bin they share: at least 80 percent of the shared bins agree within two combined standard errors and no bin differs by more than 0.3 dex

the interval of each bin (Poisson with the completeness correction, 154's counting intervals) covers a withheld half of the sample's function at the stated level on 200 seeded half-sample splits: the share of bin-splits covered lies within a 3-sigma binomial band of the level, at 0.6827
the function is refused (no table is returned) when the completeness correction or the K-correction is absent, in 100 of 100 attempts with either omitted

the mean luminosity of the flux-limited sample in redshift bins rises with redshift and sits above the sample's limiting luminosity at every redshift, the limiting-luminosity curve computed through the cosmology kernel and the K-correction of G3, to a stated tolerance of zero violations over the sample
